reading.body:
Eight applications that speak the Model Context Protocol make up this collection, and five of the eight are open source, Cline, Continue, Goose, VS Code's Copilot agent mode, and Zed, while three, Claude, Cursor, and Windsurf, are not.

Claude, described here as the protocol's first client family connecting local and remote MCP servers across desktop, CLI, and web, is itself closed source in this listing, even though Anthropic originated the protocol these eight clients all implement. That is a notable asymmetry, the company behind the open protocol ships a client that is not itself open, while five of the seven other implementations, built by separate companies and communities, are.

Two of the five open source clients, Cline and Continue, are coding agents that also appear in this site's coding and browser agents collection, cline with 67,304 GitHub stars and continue with 35,725, showing that MCP client support is being built into tools that already had an established user base rather than only into purpose-built MCP applications.
